chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

It was said to him: Indeed, Abu al-Khattab narrates from you that you said to him: 'When you know the truth, do what you will.' He said: 'May Allah curse Abu al-Khattab, by Allah I did not say to him thus, but I said: When you know the truth, do what you will of the good that is accepted from you,'

Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Whoever does righteous work, whether male or female, while being a believer, those will enter Paradise and be provided for therein without reckoning.' And He, the Blessed and Exalted, says: 'Whoever does righteous work, whether male or female, while being a believer, We will surely give him a good life.'

key_terms.أبو الخطاب: Abu al-Khattab, a companion known for narrating from the Imams
key_terms.خير يقبل منك: Good that is accepted from you
key_terms.يُرْزَقُونَ فِيهَا بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ: They will be provided for therein without reckoning

ai.seo_question: What is the correct interpretation of the phrase 'When you know the truth, do what you will' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this clarification in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* to resolve the theological tension between the Ismaili-leaning 'Abd al-Khattab al-Kufi and the Ahl al-Bayt, emphasizing that 'doing what you will' is not arbitrary license but is strictly bounded by divine acceptance of righteous deeds. This nuance safeguards the concept of *Amal* (action) within Shia jurisprudence, linking it directly to the Quranic promise of a 'good life' (*Hayat Tayyibah*) for those whose faith is manifested in valid deeds.

en.basel-kadem: 25.	We were told by Muhammed bin Musa bin Mutawakkil, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Yahya al-‘Attar, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Yunus bin Abdul-Rahman, from Ali bin Asbat, from his paternal uncle, Ya’qoub bin Salem, from Abu Baseer, that he said:
I said to Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him: Indeed, the people are saying that the Throne shook due to the death of Sa’d bin Mu’adh. He said: It is only (referring to) the bed on which he was.
